1xrkhn4:566: GPT-Realtime-Translate costs $0.034 per minute, about RMB 0.25. Human simultaneous interpreters, based on an 8-hour workday, cost roughly 25 to 44 yuan per minute — AI translation costs about one-hundredth of human interpretation. Simultaneous interpretation is widely recognized as the most difficult, highest-barrier, and highest-paying role in the translation industry. Work pressure is extreme — the interpreter must simultaneously perform five actions: listening, understanding, memorizing, translating, and speaking, and must rotate every 15 to 20 minutes because the brain runs at full capacity during interpretation. At the 2009 UN General Assembly, Libyan leader Gaddafi delivered a 96-minute speech instead of the scheduled 15 minutes; his Arabic interpreter, after holding on for 75 minutes, completely broke down, abandoned the translation on the spot, and shouted "I can't take it anymore". The training barrier for simultaneous interpreters is also extremely high: UN recruitment requires English, French, Russian, and Spanish interpreters to be proficient in at least three UN official languages, and pass a six-speech simultaneous interpretation exam (no script, covering various topics, different speeds and accents); Beijing Language and Culture University's interpreting program admits only 15 students per year, with three semesters of brutal training. There are only around 2,000 professional simultaneous interpreters worldwide, and only about 30 top-tier ones in China. The difference with OpenAI's release this time is that it turned real-time translation into a standardized API at RMB 0.25 per minute, allowing any developer to integrate easily, skipping the lab demo stage entirely, and turning "killing simultaneous interpretation" into a low-cost product deployable at scale. ByteDance's Doubao interpretation and iFlytek's interpretation had similar technology before, but OpenAI's brand influence and pricing strategy will accelerate this change.
